title: Moiré Quantum Layer Hall Effect
authors: Jin-Xin Hu, Wen-Bo Dai, X. C. Xie
abstract: Even-layer topological antiferromagnetic thin films such as MnBi$_2$Te$_4$ exhibit an unconventional layer Hall effect (LHE) arising from a layer-locked Berry curvature. This effect manifests as a layer-polarized anomalous Hall effect that can be controlled by a vertical displacement field. However, achieving a quantized version of the LHE remains experimentally challenging. In this work, we propose that moiré engineering, using an electrostatic superlattice potential from control layers, can realize the quantum layer Hall effect (QLHE). Specifically, by placing moiré control layers in close proximity to the surfaces of a MnBi$_2$Te$_4$ thin film without breaking $PT$ symmetry, the resulting system exhibits a vanishing net Hall conductance but a quantized layer Hall conductance of $e^2/h$. A weak gate electric field then breaks $PT$ symmetry and drives the system into a layer-polarized quantum anomalous Hall (QAH) phase. Furthermore, when a single control layer is introduced on only one surface, the layer-polarized QAH emerges even in the absence of an external electric field. We identify the microscopic origin of the QLHE as an emergent layer-$U(1)$ gauge field generated by the scalar moiré potential, which in turn produces opposite periodic pseudomagnetic fields on the top and bottom layers. Our work provides a feasible pathway toward realizing the QLHE in antiferromagnetic thin films.
summary: This work proposes using moiré engineering on topological antiferromagnetic films like MnBi2Te4 to realize the Quantum Layer Hall Effect (QLHE). By controlling the interlayer coupling via an electric field, the system can be driven into a layer-polarized Quantum Anomalous Hall (QAH) state. This provides a feasible, electrically tunable pathway to observe quantized topological transport in compensated magnetic materials.
main_problem: The primary goal is to achieve a quantized version of the Layer Hall Effect (LHE), termed the Quantum Layer Hall Effect (QLHE), in topological antiferromagnetic (AFM) thin films that lack net magnetization.
main_result: Moiré engineering using electrostatic superlattices allows for the realization of the QLHE, which can be driven into a layer-polarized Quantum Anomalous Hall (QAH) phase by applying a weak electric field.
method: The study uses theoretical modeling involving the construction of an effective Hamiltonian incorporating a moiré superlattice potential and calculating layer-resolved topological invariants like the Chern number.
model_or_system: The system is based on even-layer topological AFM thin films, specifically MnBi2Te4, engineered with moiré control layers creating an electrostatic superlattice potential. The physics is analyzed using a two-surface model Hamiltonian.
key_observables: Layer-resolved Chern number ($C_i$), quantized layer Hall conductance ($\sigma_{lxy} = e^2/h$), and the topological magnetoelectric response ($\alpha$).
important_parameters: The interlayer coupling strength ($\Delta z$), the moiré potential strength ($V_0$), and the applied electric field strength are critical parameters.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the low-energy physics can be captured by an effective continuum model and that the moiré potential successfully reconstructs the band topology.
figures_summary: Figures conceptually illustrate the transition from LHE to QLHE via moiré engineering, showing the resulting layer-polarized QAH state upon electric field application.
paper_structure: The paper develops the theory by introducing the moiré potential, calculating the layer-resolved Chern number, demonstrating the quantization of the LHE into QLHE, and finally showing how an external electric field drives the system into a controllable QAH phase.
why_interesting: The concept of emergent gauge fields and topological quantization in engineered magnetic systems is highly relevant to understanding topological phases in artificial quantum materials, which can be studied using advanced theoretical techniques.

(b) Upon quantization, the opposite layer Hall responses evolve into counter-propagating chiral edge states localized on opposite layers, giving rise to the QLHE.
